newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Monday.
Dealers said volume was thin throughout the day, with the tone remaining biddish on swaps after Bank Negara Malaysia imposed foreign exchange controls.

The Malaysian authority said banks were required with effect from Monday to observe a limit of $2.0 million on outstanding non-commercial related ringgit offer side swap transactions with each foreign customer on a group basis.
Dealers said fears of similar measures in Indonesia kept the underlying tone biddish in the swap market.
They said, however, rises were limited as offshore players seemed to have already established long swap positions.
Short-term swaps were firmer on the back of tight liquidity in the money market. Overnight swap was at 0.7/0.8 and tom/next at 0.6/0.7 points.
Although overnight rates eased to 15.0 percent from a high of 23.0 percent in the morning, operators remained cautious as the central bank was expected to sustain its tight policy.
"I don't expect any changes in the short-term until the foreign exchange market finds some stability," one said.
The central bank kept its short-term rates of bilateral SBIs at an artificially high level to contain speculative dollar buying using cheap rupiah.
Dealers said the rupiah appeared to be stabilising within the 2,595-2,610 range. Spot rupiah settled at 2,603/05 at 0930 GMT against an opening of 2,590/95.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,602.25/05.00 and 2,602.0/03.0, respectively.
"Sentiment on the rupiah is still mixed. People are waiting for the outcome of the Thai stability package on Tuesday," one local bank dealer said.
Thailand is holding a meeting with International Monetary Fund to work out a package to revive its ailing economy. A final agreement is expected to be submitted for cabinet approval on Tuesday.
The central bank did not offer repos on SBIs and was absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market on Monday.

The central bank offered overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, two-to-four day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
One-month swap was at 22.0/23.5, two at 42.0/43.0, three at 60.0/63.0 and six at 118.0/125.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,580/2,628 on Monday from 2,585/2,633 on Friday.
